reason: Cryptographic hash determinism is a foundational assumption for all digest properties. blake3 is audited and well-known. No internal verification planned. Compensating evidence: proptest determinism tests (PO-PROPTEST-003) catch determinism violations at integration level.
String bytes are deterministic for same String value. Guaranteed by Rust language semantics. All digest harnesses rely on this for prompt and timeout hashing.

The sentinel b"no_timeout" (for None timeout) and b"timeout" prefix (for Some timeout) are designed to not collide. Verified by PO-PROPTEST-002 (proptest, 1000 random cases, PASS) for the None-vs-Some distinction. PO-KANI-004 harness exists but blocked by blake3 inline assembly (known Kani tooling limitation tracked at github.com/model-checking/kani/issues/2). Proptest provides compensating evidence. Alternative (length-delimited encoding) deferred to future bead.

parse_ask() guarantees prompt: String and timeout: Option<String>. Digest functions assume these invariants without re-validating. If the YAML parser were to produce malformed Ask primitives, the digest path would receive malformed inputs.

Set/Finish regression tests (delegated to test-planner State 8) depend on captured digest values from before the fix. These must be captured in the test setup. Not a formal verification dependency for the current proof-obligation set.

The active path (part_05.rs) and legacy path (compile/mod.rs) must both receive the same Ask arm addition. Parity test (delegated to S8) enforces this. If only one copy is fixed, INV-ASK-006 is violated.

Fuzz target must safely reconstruct a valid WorkflowSource from arbitrary bytes. Invalid inputs must be rejected gracefully (return, not panic). The fuzz target uses String::from_utf8_lossy and bounds input to 4096 chars for prompts and 256 chars for timeouts. panic::catch_unwind guards the WorkflowSource construction.
